# A digit after a COMPLETED escape is just a character.
# A LineContinuation belongs to the STRING grammar only: it adds nothing to
# a string literal's value, and is not a token separator anywhere else.
# The string spans the lines it is written on, so a continuation keeps the
# row and column of every later token and every error: the position cells
# counts a row at LF, LS and PS, so at CRLF too, and never at a lone CR,
# inside a string or out. The first three rows are the issue's table, the
# Only an odd run of backslashes escapes the line break: two before a CRLF
# are an escaped backslash and then a real line break, which a string may
# not hold; three are an escaped backslash and a continuation.
# A continuation is an escape of its own, so it cannot complete a \x or \u
# escape it interrupts, and it is no code unit, so the two halves of a
# surrogate pair written around one are still one character. An error
# after one is sited where it stands, and one does not hide a forbidden
# escape from the check that refuses it.
